title: Course learning and discussion
summary: Enrolled learners navigate course modules, use the shared module conversation and kind-specific workbench, and prove applied knowledge through recoverable, trustworthy content challenges.

includes: Course content map and lesson reader
Read state, reactions and lesson discussion
Embedded challenge and result route family
Course learning home with progress, next actions and learning signals
A generic learning-module aggregate with exactly one required kind
A shared conversation frame present in every module
An open set of kind-specific workbenches, with document, spreadsheet and calendar as examples
A recoverable content-challenge journey covering briefing, draft, submit, evaluation, result, retry and history
Deterministic challenge validation combined with rubric-constrained AI evidence and server-authoritative finalization
Progressive challenge hints and realistic post-fidelity AI-model UAT
Authored Challenge taxonomy with prerequisites, scored requirements, guided steps, expected outputs, progressive hint and one or more typed deliverables
Learner-owned grading-model selection from the eligible catalog, bound to the immutable attempt without changing rubric authority
Exact-revision UI fidelity and signed-in desktop/mobile journey UAT before delivery can be declared complete
excludes: The persistence strategy used to implement module inheritance
Changing an existing module from one kind to another
Mock interview, flashcard or quick-quiz journeys
Global Chat and standalone Playground behavior
Course purchase or enrollment policy changes
AI provider, deployment topology and authoring-studio redesign

flows.title: Recoverable content challenge
flows.trigger: An authenticated learner with course access opens a challenge attached to course content.

steps.action: Open the exact Challenge and inspect prerequisites, scored requirements, guided steps, expected outputs, hint policy, rubric and attempt history
steps.result: The learner understands the authored task structure, required evidence and availability without repeated or flattened content

steps.action: Complete one or more typed deliverables, choose an eligible grading model and save a recoverable draft
steps.result: Every deliverable value and the learner model choice are resumable without replacing a submitted attempt

steps.action: Review the exact deliverables, selected grading model and submission effects before confirming
steps.result: The reviewed snapshot is explicit and confirmation creates one immutable submission intent

steps.action: Confirm and submit the reviewed draft once
steps.result: One immutable attempt version enters deterministic validation and rubric-constrained evaluation with the selected model

steps.action: Inspect criterion evidence, gaps, uncertainty, model identity and the next learning action
steps.result: A server-authoritative passed, needs-revision or evaluation-unavailable result is visible

steps.action: Start a new attempt from the result or resume an interrupted evaluation
steps.result: A new draft or resumed evaluation preserves prior immutable attempt and result history

outcomes: The learner proves applied course knowledge through a recoverable attempt and receives trustworthy evidence-linked feedback for the next learning action

rules.statement: A lesson can settle as pending, ready, locked or failed and exposes independently settling source, reaction and discussion regions.
Read state and comments require authenticated course access guards.
Every learning module has exactly one required kind.
Chat is a shared capability of every learning module and is not one module kind; document, accounting or spreadsheet, scheduling or calendar, and future kinds identify workbench behavior.
Shared module identity, ordering, lifecycle and conversation frame remain common while exactly one module kind owns the additional workbench state, behavior and learner presentation.
Adding a future module kind must not redefine the business contract of the base learning-module aggregate.
Opening any module mounts one shared conversational shell and exactly one workbench resolved from its kind registry entry.
Challenge access requires authenticated course access and direct-route entry cannot bypass eligibility.
Each challenge attempt binds the exact learner, challenge and rubric revisions while draft and submitted versions remain distinct.
Challenge submission is idempotent and never silently destroys or replaces the learner draft.
Deterministic validation owns objective checks; AI evaluates only declared rubric criteria that require semantic judgment.
AI output is advisory evidence and platform policy alone finalizes pass, needs-revision, evaluation-unavailable and learner progress.
Challenge feedback binds each criterion to attempt evidence, the observed gap, uncertainty and a next action without inventing evidence or exposing hidden data.
Hints are progressive and cannot reveal a complete solution before completion unless the authored challenge policy explicitly permits it.
Prompt injection, irrelevant learner content and embedded instructions cannot change the challenge rubric, authority, tools or data boundary.
Timeout, provider failure, malformed output or low confidence settles as evaluation-unavailable with safe recovery and never consumes a retry or fabricates a score.
Retry creates a new attempt version while preserving prior submissions, feedback and finalization history.
Challenge result and progress transitions are auditable and finalize once under duplicate, concurrent or resumed requests.
Locale and answer style may change explanation language but not rubric meaning or outcome.

A Challenge definition preserves prerequisites, scored requirements, guided steps, expected outputs, hint policy and one or more typed deliverables as distinct authored groups; absent optional groups are omitted rather than duplicated from the description.
The learner chooses a grading model from the currently eligible catalog; the platform may recommend Automatic but cannot silently replace an explicit learner choice.
The selected grading model and eligible-catalog revision bind the immutable attempt but cannot alter the Challenge rubric, deterministic checks, finalization policy or progress authority.

If the selected model becomes unavailable before evaluation, the attempt is preserved and settles as evaluation-unavailable with an explicit resume or choose-another-model action; no silent provider fallback is allowed.
The Challenge surface exposes one course-context breadcrumb and one exit action per action region; task copy is not repeated as briefing or deliverable guidance.
Challenge delivery remains incomplete until semantic interaction tests, exact-revision visual fidelity and signed-in desktop/mobile learner-flow UAT all pass.

acceptance.statement: Course home, content map, lesson, embedded challenge/result and course Q&A routes mount the declared learning surfaces.
Authenticated learners can persist lesson read state and create top-level comments or replies on content.

The lesson workspace reuses existing nested layouts and presents the course map, centered reader, optional outline and current overlays as one composed full viewport without redesigning existing shell regions.
SCHEMA V2 lessons render every authored programming-language tab, resolve the routed locale with default-body fallback, and rebuild the on-page outline from the selected article.
Module creation is rejected when its kind is missing.
A persisted module resolves to one and only one kind-specific workbench in addition to the shared conversation frame.
Every resolved module exposes the shared conversation frame and exactly one workbench selected by its kind.
A new module kind can add a workbench contract without changing the base module or shared conversation contract.
Missing, duplicated or kind-mismatched workbench state is rejected as an invariant violation.
An eligible learner can enter the exact challenge, understand the rubric, save and resume a draft, submit once, receive a finalized result and retry without losing prior attempt history.
Every finalized result shows a platform-owned outcome and criterion-level attempt evidence, gaps, uncertainty and a concrete next learning action.
AI output cannot directly mark a challenge passed, change course progress, weaken the rubric, invoke undeclared tools or follow instructions embedded in learner content.
AI UAT covers canonical correct, semantically equivalent, partially correct, incorrect and off-topic answers with evidence-linked criterion decisions.
AI UAT covers empty, malformed, oversized, unsupported-artifact, multilingual and adversarial prompt-injection submissions without answer leakage or cross-boundary data exposure.
Timeout, provider failure, malformed structured output and low confidence produce evaluation-unavailable, preserve the submitted attempt, do not consume a retry and expose a safe resume action.
Duplicate submissions, duplicate evaluation callbacks, concurrent finalization and interrupted resume settle idempotently to one auditable result and one progress transition.
Equivalent answers receive materially consistent rubric outcomes across supported locales while explanatory wording may vary.
Product UAT begins only after implementation fidelity passes and proves the complete Challenge journey with keyboard operation and the approved responsive layouts.

The Challenge brief renders authored prerequisites, scored requirements, guided steps, expected outputs and hint policy as distinct groups, omits absent optional groups and never manufactures them by repeating the description.
Every authored deliverable renders once with its own input, validation, draft state and score contribution; a Challenge may contain more than one deliverable.

The learner can choose an eligible grading model, review that choice with the exact deliverables and confirm one immutable submission; Automatic is a recommendation, not a forced or silent substitution.
A selected-model outage preserves the attempt and offers explicit recovery without consuming a retry or silently changing models.
The Challenge route shows the full course breadcrumb, one exit affordance per action region, no unapproved header model control and no repeated task copy across header, brief and deliverables.
Unit and integration tests prove authored-group mapping, multi-deliverable editing, model ownership, review confirmation, idempotent submission, async status, result history and recovery semantics.

Delivery cannot report ready or complete until exact-revision visual fidelity and signed-in desktop/mobile UAT complete lesson entry, rich brief inspection, evidence editing, model selection, review, immutable confirmation, grading or recovery, result, history and return to course.

evidence.claim: The course content home route mounts the content-map page for displayId.
The dynamic module/content route mounts CourseLearnContentPage.
The lesson page defines pending/ready/locked/failed states, reading/source/challenge faces, reactions, discussion, progress and outline data/actions.
The embedded challenge route mounts the challenge page.
The embedded challenge result route mounts the result page.
The course Q&A route mounts CourseQaPage.
The guarded markContentAsReaded mutation changes a learner's read state for content.
The guarded createComment mutation creates a top-level comment or reply on content.
The bare course learn route mounts CourseLearnTodayPage for the course display id.
The connected course home composes progress, ranked next actions and learning signals with independently settling states and course destinations.
The owner accepted composed reader revision 340a6bdeede7cc5dfbae0841fd54930fb1de9288c8f918e260cb96827f107ece, then explicitly authorized the seven-file SCHEMA V2 language-body corrective boundary.
The authenticated lesson query selects the legacy scalar body and every SCHEMA V2 programming-language body with locale translations.
The connected lesson reader orders language bodies, preserves a valid language choice, resolves the routed locale with authored fallback, and derives the page outline from the selected markdown.

The owner confirmed that the platform will support many modules, every module has exactly one kind, chatbot and document are only the first kinds, and the model must scale through inheritance rather than permanent hard-coded branches.

The owner clarified that every learning module includes the shared chat frame, while the module kind selects an additional workbench; accounting or spreadsheet, scheduling or calendar, document and future workbenches are open-set examples.

The owner approved Challenge revision f9032ac5841c61dcb4ce9a5013877945a2e8d9d630b92f95b2debc23d280e839: a recoverable course-content journey with revisioned drafts, immutable idempotent submissions, deterministic validation, rubric-constrained AI evidence, server-authoritative finalization, criterion feedback, retry and history.

The same approved Challenge revision requires realistic AI UAT across semantic correctness, partial and incorrect answers, malformed and unsupported input, multilingual equivalence, prompt injection, answer leakage, provider failure, low confidence, duplicate delivery, concurrency and recovery.
The owner explicitly corrected the Challenge design so the learner, not the platform alone, chooses the grading model; Automatic may remain the recommended option.
The routed legacy reference separates prerequisites, requirements, guided steps, expected outputs, hint and deliverables into distinct Challenge content groups.

The captured Challenge authority and implementation-fidelity request requires taxonomy preservation, exact approved structure, semantic tests and signed-in desktop/mobile learner-flow UAT before completion.
